name: Tancredo Neves International Airport
before:
The main international airport for Belo Horizonte, in the municipality of Confins, 44 km north of downtown. It is operated by BH Airport.

That distance shaped the airport's whole history. Confins opened in 1984 to relieve the city's original airport at Pampulha, but the journey into town and an expensive taxi ride meant almost nobody used it, and Pampulha stayed the airport of choice. It took 22 years to pass a million passengers. In March 2005 the state government restricted Pampulha to aircraft carrying up to 50 passengers, which forced 130 flights across to Confins and lifted traffic from 350,000 to around 3 million in a single year.

The road in has since been improved, and buses, taxis and executive shuttles all serve the airport, with a transfer available onto the Belo Horizonte metro.

Current capacity is 22 million passengers a year.

It has been named after Tancredo Neves, the president-elect who died in 1985, since September 1986.
after:
The main international airport for Belo Horizonte, in the municipality of Confins, 44 km north of the city centre. It is operated by BH Airport. Traffic reached 13.3 million passengers in 2025.

Pampulha, the city's original airport, was once the main airport of Minas Gerais. Executive and standard coaches link Confins with central Belo Horizonte.

It is named after Tancredo Neves, the president-elect who died in 1985.
